boundary: Surface rupture of the Hinagu fault (Takano-Shirahata + Hinagu segments), running NE-SW along the foot of the hills from Mifune/Uki through Hikawa to Yatsushiro JCT. In the NISAR interferogram it is the sharp NE-SW line where the NW side (Uki/Yatsushiro plain, LOS +10 to +22 cm, much of it interpolated) meets the SE hills (LOS about -5 to -25 cm). Near Yatsushiro the jump is about 20 cm over ~1.5 km and lands on the mapped rupture (Ryuho school, Yatsushiro Shrine).

items.title: Fault offset 94 cm across the playground of Ryuho Elementary School
items.place: Yatsushiro City Ryuho Elementary School (八代市立龍峯小学校), Okamachi/Kozenji-machi, Yatsushiro
items.what_it_shows: AIST field photo 10: the schoolyard's painted lines are offset 94 cm right-laterally, with a mole track pushed up along the rupture where it crosses the playground (photo taken facing north, 31 Jul 2026).
items.credit: Akai, Ota, Maruyama, Yoshimi, Azuma, Ninomiya / AIST Geological Survey of Japan (photo 10, 第5報)
items.licence: GSJ Terms of Use (CC BY 4.0 compatible)
items.notes: Coordinates are the school's OSM point; the rupture crosses the schoolyard, so it is within ~100 m. The search summary also mentions structural cracking at Ryuho school (unverified); the GSJ caption is the verified source.

items.title: Yatsushiro Shrine (Myoken-gu) torn by the fault: approach path offset 95 cm
items.place: Yatsushiro Shrine / Myoken-gu (八代神社), Myoken-machi, Yatsushiro
items.what_it_shows: AIST photo 12: the shrine's approach path is offset 95 cm right-laterally and dropped 39 cm on the west side. The Commons photo shows the damaged sacred gate (shinmon) a month later.
items.credit: Katorisi / Wikimedia Commons (gate photo); offset figures from AIST GSJ photo 12 (https://www.gsj.jp/hazards/earthquake/kumamoto2026/images/kumamoto2026-19.png)
items.licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Commons photo); GSJ photo: GSJ Terms of Use (CC BY 4.0 compatible)
items.notes: Do not confuse this with Yatsushiro-gū (八代宮, in the city centre near the castle). en.wikipedia says the 'Yatsushiro-gū' worship hall collapsed, which may refer to either shrine, so use only the GSJ/Commons facts here.

items.title: Expressway viaduct dropped where the rupture passes under Myoken Daiichi Bridge (Yatsushiro JCT)
items.place: Myoken Daiichi Bridge, Minami-Kyushu Expressway, just south of Yatsushiro JCT, Kamikata-machi, Yatsushiro
items.what_it_shows: en.wikipedia: 'A surface rupture propagated under a viaduct near the junction of the Kyushu Expressway and Minamikyushu Expressways, breaking along a column and causing one side to drop vertically.' AIST photo 11 shows about 130 cm of vertical offset near Yatsushiro JCT (Kamikata-machi). Commons photos show the damaged bridge piers and cracked ground around them.
items.credit: Katorisi / Wikimedia Commons; MLIT closure photo also on Commons (File:Minami Kyushu Expwy Broken Bridge after 2026 Kumamoto Earthquake (Yatsushiro JCT - Yatsushiro Minami IC).png, CC BY 4.0, 国土交通省)
items.notes: Bridge coordinates from OSM (妙見第一橋, both carriageways ~32.5020,130.6449). Katanogawa Bridge on the Kyushu Expwy (32.5025,130.6463) was also closed; its Commons photo is 'Kyushu Expressway, southbound at Katanogawa Bridge...'.

items.title: Nippon Paper Yatsushiro mill: chimney collapse killed nine, 2 km off the fault
items.place: Nippon Paper Industries Yatsushiro Mill (日本製紙八代工場), Jujo-machi, Yatsushiro
items.what_it_shows: en.wikipedia: 'In Yatsushiro, the chimney of a factory owned by Nippon Paper Industries collapsed, killing nine people and injuring two.' GSI aerial photo of the collapsed plant taken 29 Jul 2026.
items.credit: 国土地理院 (Geospatial Information Authority of Japan) via Wikimedia Commons; ground rescue photo: 総務省消防庁 (File:Rescue at NPI Yatsushiro Plant (2026 Kumamoto Earthquake).jpg, CC BY 4.0)
items.notes: The point is the centroid of the OSM industrial landuse polygon (日本製紙八代工場). The chimney's exact position inside the ~1 km site is not known, so the location is good to about 300–500 m.

items.title: AEON Mall Kumamoto: second floor collapsed with ~3,000 shoppers inside
items.place: AEON Mall Kumamoto, Kashima town (嘉島町)
items.what_it_shows: en.wikipedia: an estimated 3,000 shoppers were inside when the second floor collapsed, followed by an explosion; seven bodies and five survivors were recovered. FDMA rescue photo.
items.credit: 総務省消防庁 (Fire and Disaster Management Agency) via Wikimedia Commons; also JGSDF photo File:20260730 JGSDF Officers in AEON Mall Kumamoto after Earthquake.jpg (CC BY 4.0, 防衛省)
items.notes: The OSM bus stop 'イオンモール熊本' is at 32.7393,130.7432 and the mall building is next to it, so the location is good to about 150 m.

items.title: Kumamoto Castle: Nishi-demaru stone walls down again, 13 km from the rupture
items.place: Kumamoto Castle, Nishi-demaru, Chuo-ku, Kumamoto City
items.what_it_shows: Collapsed stone walls of the Nishi-demaru section, photographed a month after the quake (the castle was still being repaired from 2016).
items.notes: The point is the centre of the castle polygon (OSM). Nishi-demaru is the western enclosure, a few hundred metres west. The only evidence is the Commons photo and caption; the castle is not mentioned in en.wikipedia.

items.title: AEON Mall Uki: ceiling collapse right where NISAR's step crosses Ogawa
items.place: AEON Mall Uki, Ogawa-machi Minami-Ono, Uki City
items.what_it_shows: en.wikipedia: 'In Uki, parts of the ceiling at Aeon Mall Uki also collapsed.' AIST (第6報 fig. 4) found open cracks with the NW side down at the Nanbuta trench site in Ogawa (32.593,130.717, ~1 km SE) and lifted shrine foundations at Moriyama Hachimangu.
items.notes: Mall location from OSM (shop=supermarket node). No open photo of the mall damage was found. A search summary claimed a GSI DSM showing 0.5–1.0 m subsidence in a pull-apart at Ogawa, but no GSI page was fetched to confirm it, so it is not used.
